local function addTextShadow(label, transparency)
	local shadow = Instance.new("TextLabel")
	shadow.Name = "Shadow"
	shadow.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	shadow.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
	shadow.Position = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 2)
	shadow.ZIndex = math.max(1, label.ZIndex - 1)
	shadow.Text = label.Text
	shadow.TextColor3 = PALETTE.shadow
	shadow.TextTransparency = transparency or 0.35
	shadow.TextScaled = label.TextScaled
	shadow.TextSize = label.TextSize
	shadow.FontFace = label.FontFace
	shadow.TextWrapped = label.TextWrapped
	shadow.TextXAlignment = label.TextXAlignment
	shadow.TextYAlignment = label.TextYAlignment
	shadow.RichText = label.RichText
	shadow.Parent = label.Parent
	return shadow
end

local function makeShadowHost(name, size, position, z)
	local host = Instance.new("Frame")
	host.Name = name
	host.BackgroundTransparency = 1
	host.BorderSizePixel = 0
	host.Size = size
	host.Position = position
	host.ZIndex = z
	return host
end

local function attachNativeShadow(parent, size, position, z)
	local shadowHost = makeShadowHost("Shadow", size, position, z)
	local ok, uiShadow = pcall(Instance.new, "UIShadow")
	if ok and uiShadow then
		uiShadow.Color = Color3.new(0, 0, 0)
		uiShadow.Transparency = 0.72
		uiShadow.BlurRadius = UDim.new(0, 18)
		uiShadow.Offset = UDim2.fromOffset(0, 7)
		uiShadow.Parent = shadowHost
	else
		local fallback = Instance.new("ImageLabel")
		fallback.Name = "FallbackShadow"
		fallback.BackgroundTransparency = 1
		fallback.BorderSizePixel = 0
		fallback.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)
		fallback.ImageTransparency = 1
		fallback.Parent = shadowHost
	end
	shadowHost.Parent = parent
	return shadowHost
end

local function trackConnection(connection)
	table.insert(cleaners, function()
		if connection.Connected then

		end
	end)
	return connection
end

local function stopTween(key)
	local tween = activeTweens[key]
	if tween then
		tween:Cancel()
		activeTweens[key] = nil
	end
end

local function playTween(key, object, info, goal)
	stopTween(key)
	local tween = TweenService:Create(object, info, goal)
	activeTweens[key] = tween
	tween:Play()
	tween.Completed:Connect(function()
		if activeTweens[key] == tween then
			activeTweens[key] = nil
		end
	end)
	return tween
end

local function getShadowFor(control)
	local parent = control.Parent
	if not parent then
		return nil
	end
	for _, child in ipairs(parent:GetChildren()) do
		if child.Name == control.Name .. "Shadow" or child.Name == "Shadow" then
			if child:IsA("GuiObject") then
				return child
			end
		end
	end
	return nil
end

local function bindButtonEffects(button)
	local visual = button:FindFirstChild("Visual")
	local shadow = getShadowFor(button)
	local ok, controller = pcall(function()
		return ButtonEffects.bind(button, {
			visual = visual or button,
			shadow = shadow,
			sounds = false,
			hoverEnabled = true,
			hoverScale = button.Name == "PlayButton" and 1.03 or 1.025,
			pressScale = button.Name == "PlayButton" and 0.97 or 0.975,
			duration = 0.14,
			animations = true,
		})
	end)
	if ok and controller then
		table.insert(cleaners, function()
			controller:Destroy()
		end)
	end
end

	local targetOff = menuState.musicOn and 1 or 0

		thumb.Position = targetPos

	end

	playTween(toggle:GetDebugId() .. "_thumb", thumb, TweenInfo.new(0.12, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		Position = targetPos,
	})
	playTween(toggle:GetDebugId() .. "_off", offState, TweenInfo.new(0.12, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		ImageTransparency = targetOff,

	return math.clamp((inputPositionX - absPos) / absSize, 0, 1)

local Responsive = {}
function Responsive.bind(root)
    local cameraConnection
    local connections = {}
    local function update()
        local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
        if not camera then return end
        local size = camera.ViewportSize
        local mobile = math.min(size.X, size.Y) < 600
        for _, node in root:GetDescendants() do
            if node:IsA("GuiObject") then
                if node.Name == "_NexusDesktop" then node.Visible = not mobile end
                if node.Name == "_NexusMobile" then node.Visible = mobile end
            end
        end
    end
    local function observeCamera()
        if cameraConnection then cameraConnection:Disconnect() end
        local camera = workspace.CurrentCamera
        if camera then cameraConnection = camera:GetPropertyChangedSignal("ViewportSize"):Connect(update) end
        update()
    end
    table.insert(connections, workspace:GetPropertyChangedSignal("CurrentCamera"):Connect(observeCamera))
    local function cleanup()
        if cameraConnection then cameraConnection:Disconnect() end
        for _, connection in connections do connection:Disconnect() end
        table.clear(connections)
    end
    table.insert(connections, root.Destroying:Connect(cleanup))
    observeCamera()
    return cleanup

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local GuiService = game:GetService("GuiService")
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")
local ButtonFeedback = {}
local bound = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
local lastSoundAt = { hover = -math.huge, click = -math.huge }

-- Backward compatible: bind(button, childVisual) or bind(button, options).
-- Prefer options.visual = the stable button's child Visual frame.
function ButtonFeedback.bind(button, visualOrOptions, options)
    local visual
    if typeof(visualOrOptions) == "Instance" then
        visual = visualOrOptions
        options = options or {}
    else
        options = visualOrOptions or {}
        visual = options.visual or button:FindFirstChild("Visual") or button
    end
    assert(button:IsA("GuiButton"), "expected a GuiButton")
    assert(visual:IsA("GuiObject") and (visual == button or visual:IsDescendantOf(button)),
        "visual must be a child visual inside the button")
    assert(not bound[button], "button already has a feedback binding")
    assert(not visual:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale"),
        "visual UIScale already has an owner")
    local scale = Instance.new("UIScale")
    scale.Name = "FeedbackScale"
    scale.Parent = visual
    local alive, focused = true, GuiService.SelectedObject == button
    local currentTween = nil
    local shadowTween = nil
    local connections = {}
    local sounds = {}
    local originalAutoColor = button.AutoButtonColor
    button.AutoButtonColor = false
    local controller = {}
    bound[button] = controller
    local previousState = nil
    local hoverScale = math.clamp(tonumber(options.hoverScale) or 1.05, 1, 1.1)
    local pressScale = math.clamp(tonumber(options.pressScale) or 0.95, 0.85, 1)
    local duration = math.clamp(tonumber(options.duration) or 0.12, 0.06, 0.3)
    local shadow = options.shadow
    local shadowPosition = shadow and shadow.Position

    local function soundFor(kind, soundId)
        if type(soundId) ~= "string" or not soundId:match("^rbxassetid://%d+$") then return end
        local sound = Instance.new("Sound")
        sound.Name = "Feedback_" .. kind
        sound.SoundId = soundId
        sound.Volume = math.clamp(tonumber(options.volume) or 0.18, 0, 0.35)
        sound.Parent = button
        sounds[kind] = sound
    end
    soundFor("hover", options.hoverSound)
    soundFor("click", options.clickSound)

    local function playSound(kind)
        if not alive or not button.Interactable or options.sounds == false then return end
        local sound = sounds[kind]
        local now = os.clock()
        local delay = kind == "hover" and 0.12 or 0.08
        if not sound or now - lastSoundAt[kind] < delay then return end
        lastSoundAt[kind] = now
        sound.TimePosition = 0
        sound:Play()
    end

    local function pointerAvailable()
        return UserInputService.MouseEnabled
            and UserInputService:GetLastInputType() ~= Enum.UserInputType.Touch
    end

    local function refresh()
        if not alive then return end
        local state = button.GuiState
        local target = 1
        if button.Interactable then
            if state == Enum.GuiState.Press then
                target = pressScale
            elseif (state == Enum.GuiState.Hover and pointerAvailable() and options.hoverEnabled ~= false) or focused then
                target = hoverScale
            end
        end
        if state == Enum.GuiState.Hover and previousState ~= state and pointerAvailable() and options.hoverEnabled ~= false then
            playSound("hover")
        end
        previousState = state
        if currentTween then
            currentTween:Cancel()
            currentTween = nil
        end
        if shadowTween then shadowTween:Cancel() end
        if GuiService.ReducedMotionEnabled or options.animations == false then
            scale.Scale = 1
            if shadow then shadow.Position = shadowPosition end
            return
        end
        currentTween = TweenService:Create(scale,
            TweenInfo.new(duration, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out),
            { Scale = target })
        currentTween:Play()
        if shadow then
            local offset = state == Enum.GuiState.Press and -2 or 0
            shadowTween = TweenService:Create(shadow, TweenInfo.new(duration),
                { Position = shadowPosition + UDim2.fromOffset(0, offset) })
            shadowTween:Play()
        end
    end

    connections[#connections + 1] = button
        :GetPropertyChangedSignal("GuiState"):Connect(refresh)
    connections[#connections + 1] = button
        :GetPropertyChangedSignal("Interactable"):Connect(refresh)
    connections[#connections + 1] = button.SelectionGained:Connect(function()
        focused = true
        refresh()
    end)
    connections[#connections + 1] = button.SelectionLost:Connect(function()
        focused = false
        refresh()
    end)
    connections[#connections + 1] = GuiService
        :GetPropertyChangedSignal("ReducedMotionEnabled"):Connect(refresh)
    connections[#connections + 1] = button.Activated:Connect(function()
        playSound("click")
    end)

    function controller:Destroy()
        if not alive then return end
        alive = false
        if currentTween then currentTween:Cancel() end
        if shadowTween then shadowTween:Cancel() end
        for _, connection in ipairs(connections) do connection:Disconnect() end
        for _, sound in pairs(sounds) do sound:Destroy() end
        bound[button] = nil
        scale:Destroy()
        pcall(function() button.AutoButtonColor = originalAutoColor end)
        if shadow then pcall(function() shadow.Position = shadowPosition end) end
    end
    connections[#connections + 1] = button.Destroying:Connect(function()
        controller:Destroy()
    end)
    refresh()
    return controller
end

Artwork should feel polished and dimensional without clutter: Gemini-generated 9-slice skins for primary buttons and panels, matching ornamental corner pieces used sparingly, and a clean native darkened background field so the interface reads immediately. composition.focalPoint: A centered vertical stack led by the AURORA title plate above an unmistakably largest Play button, with Settings and Credits grouped directly beneath in the same dock. designPlan.artDirection: Premium fantasy-tech main menu centered on a glossy title plate and a single dominant Play call-to-action, using a controlled cyan-to-cobalt palette with thick navy framing and restrained gold edge highlights. Artwork should feel polished and dimensional without clutter: Gemini-generated 9-slice skins for primary buttons and panels, matching ornamental corner pieces used sparingly, and a clean native darkened background field so the interface reads immediately. Text remains fully live, bright, and crisp over painted surfaces. The Settings panel uses the same ornate family but in a practical layout with a readable music toggle row and a distinct volume slider track/handle set. The Credits panel is smaller and quieter, visually subordinate to the main menu. Overall mood is premium, glossy, readable, and game-ready rather than overloaded.

composition.focalPoint: A centered vertical stack led by the AURORA title plate above an unmistakably largest Play button, with Settings and Credits grouped directly beneath in the same dock. Modal panels open above the menu at center, with Settings larger and Credits compact. Decorative corners frame the composition lightly without filling the screen center.
composition.alignmentSystem: Symmetrical centered composition on desktop with a strong vertical axis; mobile reflows to a bottom-weighted centered stack to preserve thumb reach while keeping the title plate above. Comparable menu actions remain in one coherent vertical dock. Modal internals use left-aligned content rows inside centered framed windows. Consistent inset padding, mirrored ornament placement, and even button widths maintain order.

visualSystem.colorRationale: Cyan and cobalt drive the glossy fantasy-tech identity, navy provides structure and thick readable edges, and warm gold is reserved for highlights, trim, and active emphasis so it feels premium rather than noisy. Dark neutral background keeps the menu legible and prevents decorative art from overpowering the action hierarchy. Panels and controls reuse the same surface family to stay coherent.
visualSystem.outlineStyle: Thick navy outer strokes on painted controls and panels, with selective inner gold highlight lines on title plate and primary button. Native text itself is not outlined heavily; emphasis comes from contrast, weight, and controlled shadow. Use UIStroke for native supporting frames where artwork is absent.
visualSystem.shadowStyle: Short stacked shadows with dark navy bias: a soft global drop shadow under panels and title plate, plus a tighter contact shadow under buttons to reinforce press depth. Keep shadow blur moderate and opacity controlled to preserve readability on mobile.

motionSystem.hover: Hoverable controls rise slightly, brighten top gloss, and increase shadow density in a unified premium motion language. No modal container hover treatment.
motionSystem.press: Clickable controls compress with a short scale-down and 1-2px downward shift; toggle and slider parts use smaller tactile compression while preserving clarity.
motionSystem.entrance: Main menu fades and lifts in as one composition. Settings and Credits panels scale from 0.96 to 1.0 while fading in over a dimmed overlay, keeping focus at center.
motionSystem.release: Controls spring back softly to resting scale and shadow state. Panels close with a short fade and slight scale-down, while the underlying menu returns to full emphasis.
motionSystem.reducedMotion: When reduced motion is preferred, replace positional lift and scaling with opacity and gloss intensity changes only; panel open/close becomes simple fade with minimal scale delta.
motionSystem.touchBehavior: Touch devices use Activated and drag interactions only, with no synthesized hover. Press feedback occurs on touch begin and resolves on release or activation.

responsiveStrategy.desktop: Build a centered _NexusDesktop composition with a formal vertical hero stack, moderate breathing room, and panels sized for mouse precision plus controller readability. Title plate is wider, Play is visually dominant, and secondary buttons align to the same width below. Modal windows appear centered over the dock with a dim overlay and preserve ornate skins.
responsiveStrategy.mobile: Build a separate _NexusMobile composition present at build time, selected when min(viewport.X, viewport.Y)<600. Reflow into a lower-centered stack with larger width buttons and shorter vertical travel for thumb use. Decorations are simplified, title plate is compact, spacing tightens slightly, and slider/toggle hit areas enlarge. Panels stay centered but widen substantially and use stacked content for touch clarity.
responsiveStrategy.tablet: Use the mobile group for narrow tablet portrait and desktop-like spacing when width allows, but preserve the same canonical node names. Increase panel width modestly, keep the hero stack centered, and avoid over-expanding button widths beyond comfortable scan length.

implementationNotes: Create both _NexusDesktop and _NexusMobile root Frames in View.build(), each containing the same semantic nodeName descendants for title, main buttons, settings modal, and credits modal; desktop visible initially.
Use local helper functions inside View for repeated construction of glossy buttons, modal shells, title plate wrapper, and labeled settings rows.
Use a shared ButtonEffects module for hover/press/toggle/slider feedback; do not duplicate per-button controller code.
Settings and Credits modals must exist in the initial instance tree and start hidden via Visible=false or CanvasGroup transparency, then animate in the controller.
Implement actual controller behavior for open_settings_panel, close_settings_panel, open_credits_panel, and close_credits_panel by toggling the named modal containers and a dim overlay state if used.

Implement Play so it closes the menu root and fires a clearly named local hook such as OnPlayRequested via a BindableEvent or callback field owned locally by the menu module; do not invent remote networking.
Represent the required local_play_integration_hook in the build plan as the nonvisual node OnPlayRequestedHook and bind it in the controller or menu module API.
Represent the required panel_controller_behavior in the build plan as the nonvisual node PanelControllerBehavior and use it to coordinate actual settings and credits modal visibility state.
Keep live text separate from Gemini-generated artwork: title plate, panel skins, button skins, slider assets, toggle pieces, and corner ornaments are image surfaces only.
For the slider, split into stable named child parts under VolumeSlider such as TrackBack, TrackFill, Handle, and HitArea while keeping semanticAction on the parent slider component.
For the toggle, split into stable named child parts under MusicToggle such as ToggleOffState, ToggleOnState, Thumb, and HitArea while keeping semanticAction on the parent action component.
Use UIAspectRatioConstraint on painted artwork that must preserve shape, especially title plate ornaments, close icons inside compact buttons, and optional corner ornaments.
Use 9-slice behavior for component_surface and panel_surface artwork with an opaque stretchable center so live text remains readable and resizable.
Do not add any extra menu items, currencies, tabs, progression widgets, inventory, quests, shops, ranks, notifications, or rewards.
If credits content is not specified by product, provide a short live placeholder text area intended for integration, but keep it generic and within the existing Credits panel only.
No audio assets should be declared or implied because sounds were not requested; unresolved audio must remain silent.
Hover behavior should apply only on pointer-capable devices; touch uses Activated and drag without synthetic mouse enter/leave.
Use named modal overlay layers above the hero menu but beneath the active panel to dim background modestly without overpowering the painted UI.
Preserve identical icon treatment for Play, Settings, and Credits, and identical compact icon treatment for both Close buttons.
Ensure all actionable mobile controls meet or exceed 44px, with actual plan targets of 48px+ for toggle, slider, and close controls.
